title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding pages (numbered 17-18 by Grothendieck, 99-100 in the archive) try to characterize which outer or groupoid automorphisms Θ of the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(X,I) come from an element u of Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Here X is a curve over a number field K, I is a set of base points in X_{K̄}, and X is chiefly U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The previous page treated compatibility with 'structures à bout' (tangential, or punctured local, base points).

Paragraph 1, reading the illegible words by plausible inference: characterizing the image by the loop conditions plus a few further conditions is 'not very interesting', presumably because the result is close to tautological. Instead, through the study of the modular multiplicities (moduli stacks) M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller groups, Grothendieck says he is 'in the process of bringing out' interesting and plausible conjectures. These would be stated purely as properties of profinite groups such as π̂_{0,3}, presented by generators and relations, starting with conditions tied to M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}. In modern terms this is the program that became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂: an automorphism (λ, f) of F̂_2 subject to a 2-cycle relation (from M_{0,4}), a 3-cycle/hexagon relation (from M_{0,3} and M_{0,4}) and a pentagon relation (from M_{0,5}). It is the 'two-level principle' of the Esquisse, later realized by Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara.

Paragraph 2 restates in completed form the conditions for an automorphism Θ of Π̂_1(X,I), with I ∩ X_K ≠ ∅ (a K-rational base point), to come from some u ∈ Γ:
1) Loop (inertia) conditions. Θ sends each loop around a puncture or cusp to a conjugate of its χ(u)-th power, where χ is the cyclotomic character. He calls this 'surely the most important of all, by far'.
2) Stability conditions for finite étale covers X' → X defined over K (presumably K-connected). Θ must lift to Π̂_1(X', I') with I' = X'|I.

The next page continues with condition 3), stability of kernels of π̂_1(X',x') → π̂_1(Y,f(x')) for morphisms f: X' → Y. It then gives condition 4), compatibility of the induced actions with arbitrary morphisms X'_1 → X'_2 between covers, not necessarily over X. Altogether this is a 'tower/category of all covers' characterization of the image of Galois.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page states a program and lists conditions without claims of proof.

The conditions as listed are necessary conditions. Whether they are sufficient, i.e. whether they cut out exactly the image of Γ, is left open. Pop's later work shows sufficiency for suitable 'all covers' variants, while sufficiency for the GT̂-type (M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}) conditions is still open.

ideas.what: State conjectures on the Galois image purely as properties of profinite groups such as π̂_{0,3}, presented by generators, starting from relations attached to M_{0,4} and M_{0,5} (the Teichmüller tower).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂; two-level principle (2-cycle, hexagon and pentagon relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) as program; Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1990-91) for the construction of GT̂
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Loop/inertia conditions: Θ maps cusp loops to conjugates of their χ(u)-power; called by far the most important condition.
ideas.where_published: implicit in Esquisse and in the 1983 letter to Faltings

ideas.what: Characterize the Galois image by requiring that Θ lift compatibly to all finite étale covers defined over K (and, on the next page, compatibility with arbitrary morphisms between covers).
ideas.where_published: unsure; the spirit is in Esquisse, but this explicit list of conditions is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Working with the fundamental groupoid on a set I of base points containing a K-rational point, rather than with the group.
ideas.modern_name: profinite fundamental groupoid with several (tangential) base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 groupoids); Deligne (1989) tangential base points

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly juxtaposes two characterizations of the Galois image in Out(π̂_{0,3}), probably before 1984. One is the 'covers tower' characterization (loop conditions plus stability under all K-defined étale covers and morphisms between them). The other is the 'Teichmüller tower' characterization (relations coming from M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}). He judges the first relatively uninteresting compared with the second. The covers-based route is essentially what Pop later proved (I/OM and finite tripod variants), while the GT̂ route remains conjectural. This early framing of the two as alternatives is a documented precursor of Pop's line of work.
missed.quote: Mais il me semble que via l'étude des multiplicités M_{g,ν} et des groupes de Teichmüller, je suis en train de [dégager] des conjectures intéressantes et plausibles, en termes de propriétés de groupes profinis tels que π̂_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that Grothendieck anticipated the I/OM-style characterization, and it bears on the open question whether GT̂ equals G_Q. It indicates he saw the covers conditions as the 'tautological' baseline against which the M_{0,4}/M_{0,5} conditions should be compared.

missed.claim: The explicit list of conditions 1)-4) (loops, lifting to K-covers, kernel stability for maps to Y, compatibility with arbitrary morphisms between covers) is a precise sufficiency conjecture. It is never stated as such in the published Esquisse.
missed.quote: Je pense en venir encore une fois, sous forme complétée, les conditions pour un automorphisme Θ ... provenant d'un u∈Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A comparison of exactly these conditions with Pop's finite tripod hypotheses could show whether Grothendieck's list is already sufficient, possibly with fewer hypotheses.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early, probably pre-Esquisse, record of the Teichmüller-tower/GT̂ program and of a covers-based characterization of Galois anticipating I/OM. The program itself is well known from the Esquisse and the attributions are standard; only the explicit juxtaposition and the list of conditions are a mildly notable unpublished detail.
